small_guidance:
- Enable TF32 in `tl.dot` (`allow_tf32=True`) — the GEMM is 1024×8192×8192 and currently runs at fp32; TF32 will roughly double throughput on the 4090 and is well within the 5e-2 tolerance.
- Add larger autotune configs aimed at this big square GEMM (e.g. `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3` and `BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32`), and drop the small `BLOCK_N=64` configs which won't be selected at N=8192.
- Pre-transpose B once into a `[K,N]` row-major buffer cached on the module (recompute only when weight changes) so the hot loop loads B contiguously along N without strided access through `w.t()`.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite the GEMM epilogue path so groupnorm reductions run *in the same kernel* as the GEMM when possible: have each program compute a full row-tile slice of N covering an integer number of groups (group_size = 32 here), do hardtanh+mish, then warp-reduce mean/var across the group lanes and write normalized output. This removes the second full read/write of the 1024×8192 activation tensor.
- Alternatively, split into two kernels but make the groupnorm a *persistent* per-(row,group) kernel that reads the post-mish tile directly from L2: produce the GEMM output in `channels_last`-like layout where one group's 32 contiguous channels fit in a single 128B transaction, and let one warp handle a (row, group) pair.
- Consider keeping the fused GEMM emit its post-activation tile to shared memory and doing the 32-wide group reduction immediately in-register before the global store, eliminating the entire second kernel launch.
